A prover reacts to a new beacon block, constructs the corresponding\n+   `NewPayloadRequest`, and calls\n+   `proof_engine.request_proofs(new_payload_request, ProofAttributes(proof_types))`\n+   to initiate proof generation for its configured `proof_types` on the proof node.\n+2. The proof node produces an `ExecutionProof` for each requested type.\n+   The prover signs each proof using the `DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF` domain, wraps it in\n+   a `SignedExecutionProof`, and broadcasts it on the `execution_proof`\n+   topic.\n+3. Proof-verifying peers receive the gossip message, run the gossip\n+   validation rules, then call `proof_engine.verify_execution_proof` on\n+   the inner `ExecutionProof` to confirm payload validity.\n+\n+**Sync support requirement.** Independent of the request/produce/verify\n+loop above, every proof-aware node MUST retain valid proofs for\n+canonical-chain blocks back to the finalized checkpoint so that peers\n+syncing or filling gaps can backfill them via `ExecutionProofsByRange`\n+and `ExecutionProofsByRoot` (see [Req/resp domain](#reqresp-domain) for\n+the protocol details).\n+\n+#### Proof types and containers\n+\n+The consensus layer introduces a small set of new types and constants to\n+identify proofs, bound their size, and route gossip signatures:\n+\n+| Name                               | Value                      |\n+| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------- |\n+| `ProofType`                        | `uint8`                    |\n+| `MAX_PROOF_SIZE`                   | `409600` (= 400 KiB)       |\n+| `MAX_EXECUTION_PROOFS_PER_PAYLOAD` | `uint64(4)`                |\n+| `DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF`           | `DomainType('0x0D000000')` |\n+\n+`MAX_PROOF_SIZE` is set at `400 KiB` as a network-bandwidth budget: at the\n+gossip target of one proof per `(payload, proof_type)` and the cap of\n+`MAX_EXECUTION_PROOFS_PER_PAYLOAD = 4` proof types per payload, the\n+worst-case in-flight proof bandwidth per slot is `4 × 400 KiB = 1.6 MiB`\n+— of a similar order to existing per-slot blob-sidecar traffic. This\n+bounds steady-state traffic. Provers using systems that naturally\n+produce larger proofs are expected to apply proof compression\n+(recursion, succinct wrappers) before gossiping.\n+\n+Peers advertise their supported proof types via\n+`ExecutionProofStatus` (see [Req/resp domain](#reqresp-domain)). The set\n+of `proof_types` a node speaks is a per-node, dynamic configuration; new\n+proof systems can be added by socializing a new `ProofType` value\n+out-of-band and rolling it out to consenting operators. Because this EIP\n+is opt-in and changes no consensus rules, adding, deprecating, or\n+swapping proof systems does **not** require a hard fork or coordinated\n+client release — peers simply discover which proof types overlap during\n+their `ExecutionProofStatus` handshake and route requests accordingly.\n+\n+The top-level gossip message is the `SignedExecutionProof`:\n+\n+```python\n+class SignedExecutionProof(Container):\n+    message: ExecutionProof\n+    validator_index: ValidatorIndex\n+    signature: BLSSignature\n+```\n+\n+Its inner `ExecutionProof` couples a serialized proof blob to the proof\n+system and guest program it was generated against, and to the public\n+input that identifies the payload it certifies:\n+\n+```python\n+class ExecutionProof(Container):\n+    proof_data: ByteList[MAX_PROOF_SIZE]\n+    proof_type: ProofType\n+    public_input: PublicInput\n+\n+\n+class PublicInput(Container):\n+    new_payload_request_root: Root\n+    successful_validation: bool\n+    chain_config: ChainConfig\n+```\n+\n+The fields play the following roles:\n+\n+- `proof_data` is the proof system's serialized output. It is the only field\n+  whose size scales with the prover output and is bounded by\n+  `MAX_PROOF_SIZE`.\n+- `proof_type` selects which proof system and guest program the verifier dispatches to.\n+- `public_input.new_payload_request_root` is the SSZ `hash_tree_root` of the\n+  Engine API `NewPayloadRequest` whose execution this proof certifies. It is\n+  the link between a proof and a specific execution payload; verifiers use\n+  it to bind the proof to the payload they are verifying.\n+- `public_input.successful_validation` is `True` if the guest program\n+  accepted the payload as valid. Verifiers MUST check this field is\n+  `True` before treating the proof as a positive validity attestation.\n+- `public_input.chain_config` pins the chain ID and fork configuration the\n+  guest was run against, preventing cross-chain replay and fork\n+  mismatch. `ChainConfig` is defined in the\n+  [Execution Layer](#execution-layer) section.\n+- `validator_index` and `signature` identify the prover and prove that they\n+  signed the proof under `DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF`, allowing peers to\n+  attribute invalid proofs to a specific active validator.\n+\n+#### Proof engine interface\n+\n+The `ProofEngine` interface encapsulates the proof-system-specific logic\n+so that the consensus layer stays agnostic of which proof system is in\n+use. It acts as a payload-validity oracle for the beacon node, and its\n+API shape is modelled on the Engine API to allow for seamless\n+integration into the protocol. The `ProofEngine` is realized as an\n+in-client component that maintains its own proof state and delegates\n+the cryptographic work of proof generation and verification to an\n+external proof node, mirroring the way the `ExecutionEngine` delegates\n+payload execution to the EL client. The\n+interface comprises four operations and a `ProofAttributes` type:\n+\n+```python\n+def verify_execution_proof(\n+    self: ProofEngine,\n+    execution_proof: ExecutionProof,\n+) -> bool: ...\n+\n+\n+def notify_new_payload(\n+    self: ProofEngine,\n+    new_payload_request: NewPayloadRequest,\n+) -> None: ...\n+\n+\n+def notify_forkchoice_updated(\n+    self: ProofEngine,\n+    head_block_hash: Hash32,\n+    safe_block_hash: Hash32,\n+    finalized_block_hash: Hash32,\n+) -> None: ...\n+\n+\n+@dataclass\n+class ProofAttributes:\n+    proof_types: Sequence[ProofType]\n+\n+\n+def request_proofs(\n+    self: ProofEngine,\n+    new_payload_request: NewPayloadRequest,\n+    proof_attributes: ProofAttributes,\n+) -> Root: ...\n+```\n+\n+These operations decompose into three concerns:\n+\n+- **Verification** (`verify_execution_proof`) is called on every incoming\n+  proof that passes gossip validation. The engine performs the\n+  proof-system-specific cryptographic verification and binds the result\n+  to the specific payload identified by\n+  `proof.public_input.new_payload_request_root`. A payload is considered\n+  proof-verified once `k` valid `SignedExecutionProof`s for it have been\n+  verified. The value of `k` will be pinned before this EIP transitions\n+  to `Review`; it is intentionally left open while the network gathers\n+  real-world data.\n+  Peers exchange their current proof-verification view via\n+  `ExecutionProofStatus`.\n+- **Lifecycle notifications** (`notify_new_payload`,\n+  `notify_forkchoice_updated`) keep the engine in sync with the state\n+  of the beacon node. `notify_new_payload` lets the engine associate\n+  incoming proofs with the payloads they certify;\n+  `notify_forkchoice_updated` lets it track the canonical chain to\n+  drive proof retention and pruning.\n+- **Generation** (`request_proofs`) is used by proof-generating nodes to\n+  trigger asynchronous proof generation for a given payload and set of\n+  proof types. The return value is `new_payload_request.hash_tree_root()`,\n+  which the prover uses as a request id to correlate the proof-completion\n+  SSE event the proof node emits when a proof is ready to be fetched.\n+\n+#### Beacon-chain state transition\n+\n+EIP-8025 extends `process_block` to forward execution payload processing to\n+both the execution engine and the proof engine, and introduces a new\n+`process_execution_proof` handler for incoming proofs.\n+\n+`process_block` is modified to pass `PROOF_ENGINE` to\n+`process_execution_payload`:\n+\n+```python\n+def process_block(state: BeaconState, block: BeaconBlock) -> None:\n+    process_block_header(state, block)\n+    process_withdrawals(state, block.body.execution_payload)\n+    # [Modified in EIP8025]\n+    process_execution_payload(state, block.body, EXECUTION_ENGINE, PROOF_ENGINE)\n+    process_randao(state, block.body)\n+    process_eth1_data(state, block.body)\n+    process_operations(state, block.body)\n+    process_sync_aggregate(state, block.body.sync_aggregate)\n+```\n+\n+`process_execution_payload` is modified to additionally notify the proof\n+engine of the new payload after the execution engine has accepted it.\n+This hook lets the proof engine learn of each new payload so it\n+can associate it with the proofs that certify it as they arrive over\n+gossip:\n+\n+```python\n+def process_execution_payload(\n+    state: BeaconState,\n+    body: BeaconBlockBody,\n+    execution_engine: ExecutionEngine,\n+    proof_engine: ProofEngine,\n+) -> None:\n+    ...\n+    # Verify the execution payload is valid via ExecutionEngine\n+    assert execution_engine.verify_and_notify_new_payload(\n+        NewPayloadRequest(...)\n+    )\n+\n+    # [New in EIP8025]\n+    # Notify ProofEngine of the new execution payload\n+    proof_engine.notify_new_payload(NewPayloadRequest(...))\n+    ...\n+```\n+\n+A new `process_execution_proof` handles a `SignedExecutionProof` once it has\n+passed gossip validation. It re-checks that the prover is active in the\n+current state, verifies the BLS signature under `DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF`,\n+and delegates cryptographic verification to the proof engine:\n+\n+```python\n+def process_execution_proof(\n+    state: BeaconState,\n+    signed_proof: SignedExecutionProof,\n+    proof_engine: ProofEngine,\n+) -> None:\n+    proof_message = signed_proof.message\n+\n+    # Verify prover is an active validator\n+    validator = state.validators[signed_proof.validator_index]\n+    assert is_active_validator(validator, get_current_epoch(state))\n+\n+    domain = get_domain(state, DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF, compute_epoch_at_slot(state.slot))\n+    signing_root = compute_signing_root(proof_message, domain)\n+    assert bls.Verify(validator.pubkey, signing_root, signed_proof.signature)\n+\n+    # Verify the execution proof\n+    assert proof_engine.verify_execution_proof(proof_message)\n+```\n+\n+`process_execution_proof` is invoked outside the beacon-block state-transition\n+function and produces no on-chain state change: it is the operational hook\n+that lets a node decide whether to treat a gossiped proof as a valid\n+attestation of an execution payload. Proof storage is managed by the\n+`ProofEngine`; retention is bounded by `proof_serve_range` (see\n+[Req/resp domain](#reqresp-domain)): clients MUST retain proofs for\n+canonical-chain blocks\n+back to the finalized checkpoint so they can serve `ExecutionProofsByRange`\n+and `ExecutionProofsByRoot` requests.\n+\n+#### Proof gossip\n+\n+Execution proofs are gossiped over a new global topic, `execution_proof`,\n+carrying `SignedExecutionProof` messages. Each rule below is a libp2p\n+gossipsub validation rule, following the same `[IGNORE]` / `[REJECT]`\n+conventions used by the other beacon-node gossip topics. With\n+`proof = signed_execution_proof.message`:\n+\n+- _[IGNORE]_ the proof's `new_payload_request_root` has been seen via\n+  gossip or non-gossip sources (clients MAY queue proofs until the\n+  corresponding payload arrives).\n+- _[IGNORE]_ no _valid_ proof has already been received for the tuple\n+  `(new_payload_request_root, proof_type)` — i.e. only the first valid\n+  proof of each type per payload is forwarded.\n+- _[IGNORE]_ this is the first proof received for the tuple\n+  `(new_payload_request_root, proof_type, validator_index)` — i.e. each\n+  prover gets one shot per `(payload, proof_type)`.\n+- _[REJECT]_ the validator at `validator_index` is an active validator.\n+- _[REJECT]_ the BLS signature is valid for the prover's public key under\n+  `DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF`.\n+- _[REJECT]_ `proof.proof_data` is non-empty and no larger than\n+  `MAX_PROOF_SIZE`.\n+- _[REJECT]_ all of the checks in `process_execution_proof` pass.\n+\n+These rules compose with the existing gossipsub peer-scoring machinery: a\n+peer relaying messages that hit `[REJECT]` is downscored by the same\n+mechanism that scores misbehaviour on any other CL gossip topic. The\n+`[IGNORE]` rules bound steady-state bandwidth — once a node has a valid\n+proof for a given `(new_payload_request_root, proof_type)`, additional\n+proofs for the same tuple are dropped silently, regardless of who signs\n+them.\n+\n+#### Req/resp domain\n+\n+Three req/resp protocols let peers backfill, target, and coordinate proof\n+state:\n+\n+- **`ExecutionProofsByRange`** — request `(start_slot, count, proof_types)`,\n+  response `List[SignedExecutionProof]`. Mirrors `BlobSidecarsByRange` and\n+  `DataColumnSidecarsByRange`: range-based, root-unaware, filtered by proof\n+  type. Used for bulk backfill of proofs after a syncing window.\n+- **`ExecutionProofsByRoot`** — request `List[ProofByRootIdentifier]` where\n+  each identifier carries `(block_root, List[proof_type])`, response\n+  `List[SignedExecutionProof]`. Used for targeted retrieval when a node\n+  knows the specific block roots whose proofs it is missing.\n+- **`ExecutionProofStatus`** — request and response share the same\n+  container: `(block_root, slot, proof_types)`. Peers exchange the most\n+  recent block they consider proof-verified, plus their dynamically\n+  advertised set of supported proof types. The dialing peer MUST send a\n+  status on first connecting to any proof-aware peer. This is similar in\n+  nature to the beacon-chain\n+  [`Status v2`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/031e521f0a82b0e475ecfc13f79dd251a6284fc2/specs/fulu/p2p-interface.md#status-v2)\n+  handshake.\n+\n+Clients MUST serve both range and root requests for any block on the\n+canonical chain whose slot is in `proof_serve_range` — defined as\n+`[finalized_checkpoint.slot, current_slot]`. Peers unable to reply respond\n+with `3: ResourceUnavailable` and MAY be descored. The shape of these\n+protocols composes with existing sync flows: a node syncing forward over\n+blocks pulls proofs by range; a node patching a specific gap pulls them by\n+root.\n+\n+#### Discovery\n+\n+Discovery is extended with a new Ethereum Node Record (ENR) key, `eproof`, encoded as a `uint8`. A\n+node is considered proof-aware if the field is present and non-zero,\n+allowing other peers to filter for proof-aware peers during discovery. This\n+mirrors the existing pattern used to advertise data-column awareness in\n+Fulu via the\n+[`cgc` ENR field](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/031e521f0a82b0e475ecfc13f79dd251a6284fc2/specs/fulu/p2p-interface.md#the-discovery-domain-discv5)\n+and is intentionally cheap: no fork or fork-version bump is required for a\n+node to start (or stop) advertising proof support.\n+\n+#### Prover lifecycle\n+\n+The prover lifecycle is illustrated below:\n+\n+![Prover lifecycle: SSE-driven flow between beacon node, prover, and proof node](../assets/eip-8025/prover-lifecycle.png)\n+\n+A prover's flow, as detailed in the prover guide referenced above, is\n+fully event-driven:\n+\n+1. **Subscribe to two SSE event streams** at startup:\n+   - `Block` events from the beacon node, signalling that a new valid beacon\n+     block has been received.\n+   - Proof-completion events from the proof node.\n+2. **On a `Block` event**, fetch the full `BeaconBlock` via RPC, construct\n+   the corresponding `NewPayloadRequest`, choose the `ProofAttributes`\n+   (set of `proof_types` the prover wants to generate), and call\n+   `proof_engine.request_proofs(...)`. The returned root is used to track\n+   the request.\n+3. **On a proof-completion event** matching a tracked root, fetch the\n+   completed `ExecutionProof` from the proof node, sign it under\n+   `DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF`, wrap it in a `SignedExecutionProof`, and\n+   broadcast on the `execution_proof` gossip topic.\n+\n+The signing helper is:\n+\n+```python\n+def get_execution_proof_signature(\n+    state: BeaconState, proof: ExecutionProof, privkey: int\n+) -> BLSSignature:\n+    domain = get_domain(state, DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF, compute_epoch_at_slot(state.slot))\n+    signing_root = compute_signing_root(proof, domain)\n+    return bls.Sign(privkey, signing_root)\n+```\n+\n+The prover role is scoped to the optional-proof phase. If a future EIP\n+were to make execution proofs mandatory, proof generation would\n+plausibly move into block production, at which point the prover role\n+and the optional gossip topic could be deprecated in favour of\n+in-block proof commitments.\n+\n+### Execution Layer\n+\n+This EIP introduces a stateless execution guest and prover side logic to construct the input used by\n+that guest. The prover runs the guest over private `StatelessInput` bytes. The\n+proof exposes `StatelessValidationResult` as public output, allowing a verifier\n+to bind the proof to the payload request being checked.\n+\n+A proof-verifying node accepts the execution-layer result only if:\n+\n+- the proof verifies for the expected guest program;\n+- `successful_validation` is `true`;\n+- `new_payload_request_root` equals the SSZ `hash_tree_root` of the\n+  `NewPayloadRequest` associated with the payload being validated; and\n+- `chain_config` matches the chain ID and fork configuration expected by the\n+  verifier.\n+\n+At a high level, proof generation follows this flow:\n+\n+1. A host, usually a stateful execution-layer client, executes or constructs\n+   the block while recording the account, storage, code, and ancestor-header\n+   data used during execution.\n+2. The host builds an `ExecutionWitness`, wraps it with the Engine API\n+   `NewPayloadRequest`, chain configuration, and transaction public keys into a\n+   `StatelessInput`, and serializes that input as schema-prefixed SSZ bytes.\n+3. A prover runs the guest program on the serialized `StatelessInput`. The\n+   guest validates the chain configuration and witness scaffolding, executes the\n+   payload against witness-backed state, and returns `StatelessValidationResult`.\n+\n+#### Stateless input and output\n+\n+The top-level guest input is private prover input:\n+\n+```python\n+class StatelessInput:\n+    new_payload_request: NewPayloadRequest\n+    witness: ExecutionWitness\n+    chain_config: ChainConfig\n+    public_keys: Tuple[Bytes, ...]\n+```\n+\n+The guest output is public:\n+\n+```python\n+class StatelessValidationResult:\n+    new_payload_request_root: Hash32\n+    successful_validation: bool\n+    chain_config: ChainConfig\n+```\n+\n+Note this struct is the EL-counterpart of `PublicInput` described in the _Proof types and containers_\n+section.\n+\n+At this level:\n+\n+- `new_payload_request` is the Engine API payload data supplied by the\n+  consensus layer.\n+- `witness` is the account, storage, code, and ancestor-header data needed to\n+  execute the payload without local EL state.\n+- `chain_config` tells the guest which chain ID and fork configuration to\n+  validate against.\n+- `public_keys` contains one 65-byte uncompressed secp256k1 public key for\n+  each transaction signer, in the same order as the transactions in the payload.\n+  Optimized guests can use these keys to avoid public-key recovery, but\n+  transaction signatures and supplied public keys MUST still be verified.\n+\n+The `NewPayloadRequest` commits to the payload, blob versioned hashes,\n+`parent_beacon_block_root`, and typed execution requests:\n+\n+```python\n+class NewPayloadRequest:\n+    execution_payload: ExecutionPayload\n+    versioned_hashes: Tuple[VersionedHash, ...]\n+    parent_beacon_block_root: Root\n+    execution_requests: ExecutionRequests\n+\n+\n+class ExecutionPayload:\n+    parent_hash: Hash32\n+    fee_recipient: Address\n+    state_root: Root\n+    receipts_root: Root\n+    logs_bloom: Bloom\n+    prev_randao: Bytes32\n+    block_number: Uint\n+    gas_limit: Uint\n+    gas_used: Uint\n+    timestamp: U256\n+    extra_data: Bytes\n+    base_fee_per_gas: Uint\n+    block_hash: Hash32\n+    transactions: Tuple[Bytes, ...]\n+    withdrawals: Tuple[Withdrawal, ...]\n+    blob_gas_used: U64\n+    excess_blob_gas: U64\n+    block_access_list: Bytes\n+```\n+\n+The execution requests are represented as typed containers, matching the\n+consensus-layer specs:\n+\n+```python\n+class DepositRequest:\n+    pubkey: Bytes48\n+    withdrawal_credentials: Bytes32\n+    amount: U64\n+    signature: Bytes96\n+    index: U64\n+\n \n-Validators will now be able to enable two new modes:\n+class WithdrawalRequest:\n+    source_address: Address\n+    validator_pubkey: Bytes48\n+    amount: U64\n \n-- zkEVM Proof generating\n-- Stateless validation\n \n-When a proof generating node receives a beacon block, they will create the necessary proofs for the execution payload in the block and re-propagate them on the specified subnets.\n+class ConsolidationRequest:\n+    source_address: Address\n+    source_pubkey: Bytes48\n+    target_pubkey: Bytes48\n \n-When a stateless validating node receives a beacon block, they will check to see if they have already received a valid execution proof for that execution payload from the specified subnet.\n \n-The detailed specifications are in the consensus-specs repository.\n+class ExecutionRequests:\n+    deposits: Tuple[DepositRequest, ...]\n+    withdrawals: Tuple[WithdrawalRequest, ...]\n+    consolidations: Tuple[ConsolidationRequest, ...]\n+```\n \n-The key words \"MUST\", \"MUST NOT\", \"REQUIRED\", \"SHALL\", \"SHALL NOT\", \"SHOULD\", \"SHOULD NOT\", \"RECOMMENDED\", \"NOT RECOMMENDED\", \"MAY\", and \"OPTIONAL\" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119 and RFC 8174.\n+The remaining top-level fields define the witness and chain context consumed by\n+the guest:\n+\n+```python\n+class ExecutionWitness:\n+    state: Tuple[Bytes, ...]\n+    codes: Tuple[Bytes, ...]\n+    headers: Tuple[Bytes, ...]\n+\n+\n+class ChainConfig:\n+    chain_id: U64\n+    active_fork: ForkConfig\n+\n+\n+class ForkConfig:\n+    fork: ProtocolFork\n+    activation: ForkActivation\n+    blob_schedule: BlobSchedule | None\n+\n+\n+class ForkActivation:\n+    block_number: U64 | None\n+    timestamp: U64 | None\n+\n+\n+class BlobSchedule:\n+    target: U64\n+    max: U64\n+    base_fee_update_fraction: U64\n+\n+\n+class ProtocolFork(StrEnum):\n+    ...\n+    Amsterdam = \"Amsterdam\"\n+```\n+\n+The `ExecutionWitness` fields have the following roles:\n+\n+- `state`: RLP-encoded account and storage trie-node preimages needed during\n+  execution and state-root recomputation.\n+- `codes`: bytecodes required for code reads from the pre-state. Code created\n+  in the block being executed is not included because the guest observes it\n+  during re-execution.\n+- `headers`: RLP-encoded parent and ancestor headers, ordered by block number\n+  and ending at the payload parent. These headers provide the parent state root\n+  and the recent block hashes used by `BLOCKHASH` and system-contract logic.\n+  The guest checks that the headers form a contiguous chain.\n+\n+#### Guest validation\n+\n+The guest entry point decodes schema-prefixed SSZ input, runs stateless payload \n+validation, and serializes the result.\n+\n+```python\n+def run_stateless_guest(input_bytes: Bytes) -> Bytes:\n+    stateless_input = deserialize_stateless_input(input_bytes)\n+    stateless_output = verify_stateless_new_payload(stateless_input)\n+    return serialize_stateless_output(stateless_output)\n+```\n+\n+The main validation path first computes the public payload-request commitment.\n+It then validates fork configuration, checks the header witness, creates a\n+`WitnessState`, and delegates payload execution to the same `new_payload` path\n+used by the execution engine:\n+\n+```python\n+def compute_new_payload_request_root(\n+    stateless_input: StatelessInput,\n+) -> Hash32:\n+    ssz_npr = _new_payload_request_to_ssz(stateless_input.new_payload_request)\n+    return Hash32(ssz_npr.hash_tree_root())\n+\n+\n+def validate_chain_config(\n+    chain_config: ChainConfig,\n+    new_payload_request: NewPayloadRequest,\n+) -> ForkConfig:\n+    active_fork = chain_config.active_fork\n+    execution_payload = new_payload_request.execution_payload\n+\n+    if not _is_activation_active(active_fork.activation, execution_payload):\n+        raise InactiveForkConfigError(...)\n+    if active_fork.fork not in guest_supported_forks():\n+        raise UnsupportedForkConfigError(...)\n+    if active_fork.blob_schedule != _expected_amsterdam_blob_schedule():\n+        raise UnsupportedForkConfigError(...)\n+\n+    return active_fork\n+\n+\n+def validate_headers(\n+    encoded_headers: Tuple[Bytes, ...],\n+) -> Tuple[List[Header | PreviousForkHeader], List[Hash32]]:\n+    assert len(encoded_headers) <= 256\n+    headers = [_decode_header(header) for header in encoded_headers]\n+    block_hashes = [keccak256(header) for header in encoded_headers]\n+    for i in range(1, len(headers)):\n+        if headers[i].parent_hash != block_hashes[i - 1]:\n+            raise Exception(\"Witness headers are not contiguous\")\n+    return headers, block_hashes\n+\n+\n+def verify_stateless_new_payload(\n+    stateless_input: StatelessInput,\n+) -> StatelessValidationResult:\n+    new_payload_request_root = compute_new_payload_request_root(\n+        stateless_input\n+    )\n+    witness = stateless_input.witness\n+\n+    try:\n+        validate_chain_config(\n+            stateless_input.chain_config,\n+            stateless_input.new_payload_request,\n+        )\n+\n+        decoded_headers, block_hashes = validate_headers(witness.headers)\n+        parent_header = decoded_headers[-1]\n+\n+        chain_context = ChainContext(\n+            chain_id=stateless_input.chain_config.chain_id,\n+            block_hashes=block_hashes,\n+            parent_header=parent_header,\n+        )\n+\n+        pre_state = WitnessState(\n+            _node_db=build_node_db(witness.state),\n+            _state_root=parent_header.state_root,\n+            _code_db=build_code_db(witness.codes),\n+        )\n+\n+        execute_new_payload_request(\n+            stateless_input.new_payload_request,\n+            pre_state,\n+            chain_context,\n+            transaction_public_keys=stateless_input.public_keys,\n+        )\n+        successful_validation = True\n+    except Exception:\n+        successful_validation = False\n+\n+    return StatelessValidationResult(\n+        new_payload_request_root=new_payload_request_root,\n+        successful_validation=successful_validation,\n+        chain_config=stateless_input.chain_config,\n+    )\n+```\n+\n+`WitnessState` is the stateless replacement for a local pre-state database. It\n+serves account, storage, and code reads from the witness and computes the\n+post-state root from the execution diff:\n+\n+```python\n+class WitnessState:\n+    _node_db: Dict[Bytes, Bytes]\n+    _state_root: Root\n+    _code_db: Dict[Hash32, Bytes]\n+\n+    def get_account_optional(self, address: Address) -> Optional[Account]: ...\n+    def get_storage(self, address: Address, key: Bytes32) -> U256: ...\n+    def get_code(self, code_hash: Hash32) -> Bytes: ...\n+\n+    def compute_state_root_and_trie_changes(\n+        self,\n+        account_changes: Dict[Address, Optional[Account]],\n+        storage_changes: Dict[Address, Dict[Bytes32, U256]],\n+    ) -> Tuple[Root, List[InternalNode]]:\n+        ...\n+```\n+\n+The payload execution logic performs the normal payload checks before\n+executing the block:\n+\n+```python\n+def execute_new_payload_request(\n+    new_payload_request: NewPayloadRequest,\n+    pre_state: PreState,\n+    chain_context: ChainContext,\n+    transaction_public_keys: Optional[Tuple[Bytes, ...]] = None,\n+) -> Tuple[BlockDiff, Block]:\n+    payload = new_payload_request.execution_payload\n+\n+    if b\"\" in payload.transactions:\n+        raise InvalidBlock(\"Empty transaction in payload\")\n+    if not is_valid_block_hash(\n+        payload,\n+        new_payload_request.parent_beacon_block_root,\n+        new_payload_request.execution_requests,\n+    ):\n+        raise InvalidBlock(\"Invalid block hash\")\n+    if not is_valid_versioned_hashes(new_payload_request):\n+        raise InvalidBlock(\"Invalid versioned hashes\")\n+\n+    block = _payload_block(\n+        payload,\n+        new_payload_request.parent_beacon_block_root,\n+        new_payload_request.execution_requests,\n+    )\n+    block_diff = execute_block(\n+        block,\n+        pre_state,\n+        chain_context,\n+        transaction_public_keys=transaction_public_keys,\n+    )\n+    return block_diff, block\n+```\n+\n+During transaction processing, supplied public keys are verified before deriving\n+sender addresses:\n+\n+```python\n+def recover_sender_from_public_key(\n+    chain_id: U64,\n+    tx: Transaction,\n+    public_key: Bytes,\n+) -> Address:\n+    if public_key != recover_transaction_public_key(chain_id, tx):\n+        raise InvalidSignatureError\n+    return _sender_address_from_public_key(public_key)\n+```\n+\n+Optimized guests may avoid full public-key recovery, but they must still verify\n+that the supplied key validates the transaction signature and is consistent with\n+the recovery id or y-parity bit.\n+\n+#### Host-side input construction\n+\n+On the host side, `build_stateless_input` receives the artefacts gathered during\n+block execution or construction and packages them for the guest:\n+\n+```python\n+def build_stateless_input(\n+    block: Block,\n+    *,\n+    execution_witness: ExecutionWitness,\n+    execution_requests: ExecutionRequests,\n+    block_access_list: BlockAccessList,\n+    chain_id: U64,\n+) -> StatelessInput:\n+    ...\n+\n+    new_payload = NewPayloadRequest(\n+        execution_payload=payload,\n+        versioned_hashes=tuple(versioned_hashes),\n+        parent_beacon_block_root=header.parent_beacon_block_root,\n+        execution_requests=execution_requests,\n+    )\n+\n+    return StatelessInput(\n+        new_payload_request=new_payload,\n+        witness=execution_witness,\n+        chain_config=build_chain_config(chain_id),\n+        public_keys=tuple(public_keys),\n+    )\n+```\n+\n+The host also provides the fork configuration corresponding to the payload being\n+validated:\n+\n+```python\n+def build_chain_config(chain_id: U64) -> ChainConfig:\n+    return ChainConfig(\n+        chain_id=chain_id,\n+        active_fork=ForkConfig(\n+            fork=ProtocolFork.Amsterdam,\n+            activation=ForkActivation(\n+                block_number=None,\n+                timestamp=U64(0),\n+            ),\n+            blob_schedule=BlobSchedule(\n+                target=BLOB_SCHEDULE_TARGET,\n+                max=BLOB_SCHEDULE_MAX,\n+                base_fee_update_fraction=U64(BLOB_BASE_FEE_UPDATE_FRACTION),","path":"EIPS/eip-8025.md","commit_id":"d5653bc4d9b86997e069567dcd1eb8766b0c8a55","original_commit_id":"d5653bc4d9b86997e069567dcd1eb8766b0c8a55","user":{"login":"jsign","id":6136245,"node_id":"MDQ6VXNlcjYxMzYyNDU=","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/6136245?v=4","gravatar_id":"","url":"https://api.github.com/users/jsign","html_url":"https://github.com/jsign","followers_url":"https://api.github.com/users/jsign/followers","following_url":"https://api.github.com/users/jsign/following{/other_user}","gists_url":"https://api.github.com/users/jsign/gists{/gist_id}","starred_url":"https://api.github.com/users/jsign/starred{/owner}{/repo}","subscriptions_url":"https://api.github.com/users/jsign/subscriptions","organizations_url":"https://api.github.com/users/jsign/orgs","repos_url":"https://api.github.com/users/jsign/repos","events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/jsign/events{/privacy}","received_events_url":"https://api.github.com/users/jsign/received_events","type":"User","user_view_type":"public","site_admin":false},"body":"Correct. Nothing here is intended to be new.","created_at":"2026-07-07T20:26:40Z","updated_at":"2026-07-07T20:29:44Z","html_url":"https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/11604#discussion_r3539438946","pull_request_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/ethereum/EIPs/pulls/11604","_links":{"self":{"href":"https://api.github.com/repos/ethereum/EIPs/pulls/comments/3539438946"},"html":{"href":"https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/11604#discussion_r3539438946"},"pull_request":{"href":"https://api.github.com/repos/ethereum/EIPs/pulls/11604"}},"reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/ethereum/EIPs/pulls/comments/3539438946/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"start_line":null,"original_start_line":null,"start_side":null,"line":866,"original_line":866,"side":"RIGHT","in_reply_to_id":3499816256,"author_association":"CONTRIBUTOR","original_position":878,"position":878,"subject_type":"line"},{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/ethereum/EIPs/pulls/comments/3539445807","pull_request_review_id":4648635348,"id":3539445807,"node_id":"PRRC_kwDOAq426M7S96gv","diff_hunk":"@@ -2,59 +2,1139 @@\n eip: 8025\n title: Optional Execution Proofs\n description: Introducing optional execution proofs on the consensus layer\n-author: Kevaundray Wedderburn (@kevaundray), Justin Drake (@JustinDrake) <justin@ethereum.org>\n+author: Kevaundray Wedderburn (@kevaundray), Justin Drake (@JustinDrake), Ignacio Hagopian (@jsign), Han (@han0110), Francesco Risitano (@frisitano)\n discussions-to: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-optional-execution-proofs/25500\n-status: Stagnant\n+status: Draft\n type: Standards Track\n category: Core\n created: 2025-09-17\n+requires: 4844, 6110, 7002, 7251, 7732, 7928\n ---\n \n ## Abstract\n \n-Optional execution proofs allow beacon nodes to verify the validity of the execution payload within a beacon block without running an execution layer client. The execution proofs are sent over the consensus layer's peer-to-peer network.\n+Execution proofs enable consensus layer (CL) nodes to perform stateless validation of execution payloads. Altruistic _proof-generating nodes_ produce execution proofs and broadcast them over the CL p2p network. _Proof-verifying nodes_ consume gossiped execution proofs to assert the validity of execution payloads. Verification is _stateless_ and sublinear in the gas limit, so a validator's resource requirements scale sublinearly, an improvement on the linear cost of re-execution. The mechanism is fully opt-in and changes no consensus rules, allowing the proving stack to mature in production; a separate, future EIP could subsequently propose making execution proofs mandatory once they have matured. This EIP does not introduce incentives for proof-generating nodes; for that reason, they are considered altruistic and the mechanism is opt-in.\n \n ## Motivation\n \n-Optional execution proofs reduce the hardware and bandwidth requirements that are needed for an attester to verify a beacon block. Moreover, the cost to verify to a block no longer grows with the gas limit.\n+Today, verifying a beacon block requires re-execution of its execution payload against the EL state — the full set of account and storage trie data. The cost of re-execution scales linearly with the gas limit. This couples a node's resource requirements to the state size and the chain's throughput.\n \n-Since these are optional, protocol upgrades cannot be based on the improvements in this EIP. This EIP allows us to safely test execution proofs without making it explicitly consensus critical.\n+This EIP introduces an opt-in path with the following properties:\n+\n+- **Sublinear verification cost.** Both verifier runtime and proof size scale as `O(log² n)` in `n`, the number of execution steps of the guest program executing the payload. `n` is bounded by the payload's gas limit.\n+- **Stateless verification.** Verifying an execution proof requires only the proof itself and a public commitment to the payload — not the EL state.\n+- **Broader verifier participation.** Sublinear, stateless verification lowers the resource floor for proof-verifying validators, keeping payload-validity checks tractable for participants with modest hardware and expertise even as the gas limit and state grow.\n+- **Optional by design.** Deploying execution proofs as opt-in lets clients and operators build operational experience, collect performance metrics, and fine-tune the proving stack against live-network conditions without enshrining untested mechanics in the protocol or impacting validators that have not opted in.\n \n ## Specification\n \n-This is a consensus layer change only. \n+The key words \"MUST\", \"MUST NOT\", \"REQUIRED\", \"SHALL\", \"SHALL NOT\", \"SHOULD\", \"SHOULD NOT\", \"RECOMMENDED\", \"NOT RECOMMENDED\", \"MAY\", and \"OPTIONAL\" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) and [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174).\n+\n+### Terminology\n+\n+This EIP uses the following proof-system terms:\n+\n+- **Proof system.** The cryptographic system used to prove that a computation was performed correctly. Different proof systems may have different proof formats, verifier logic, proving costs, and security assumptions.\n+\n+- **Prover.** A node that runs the execution-validation computation and produces an execution proof attesting to the result. In this EIP, provers are opt-in, altruistic proof-generating validators.\n+\n+- **Verifier.** A node that checks an execution proof instead of re-executing payload validation.\n+\n+- **Guest.** The program whose execution is being proven. Here, the guest program performs stateless validation of an execution payload.\n+\n+- **Host.** The off-chain logic that prepares the guest input, runs the guest inside the proof system, and packages the resulting proof.\n+\n+- **Private input.** Data supplied to the guest by the prover but not revealed to verifiers. In this EIP, the serialized `StatelessInput` is private input: it contains the data needed to run stateless payload validation.\n+\n+- **Execution Witness.** The execution data within the private input that lets the guest validate the payload without the verifier holding the full EL state.\n+\n+- **Public input.** The data committed to by the proof and visible to verifiers. In this EIP, the public input binds the proof to a specific `NewPayloadRequest`, chain configuration, and validation result.\n+\n+- **Proof node.** An external component that performs proof-system-specific work such as proof generation and proof verification.\n+\n+- **Proof engine.** The consensus-client interface used to communicate with a proof node. The `ProofEngine` keeps the consensus-layer integration proof-system-agnostic.\n+\n+- **Proof-aware peer.** A consensus-layer peer that advertises optional execution-proof support and participates in the execution-proof networking protocols for its supported proof types.\n+\n+- **Server-Sent Events (SSE).** An HTML standard for one-way, long-lived HTTP event streams from server to client. In this EIP, SSE is used in two places: by the beacon node to push `Block` events to the prover, and by the proof node to push proof-completion events to the prover.\n+\n+### Specification references\n+\n+The normative specifications for this EIP are maintained alongside the rest of the protocol in the consensus-specs and execution-specs repositories. The sections below summarise the changes; the canonical sources are:\n+\n+- [Consensus Layer](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/tree/031e521f0a82b0e475ecfc13f79dd251a6284fc2/specs/_features/eip8025)\n+- Execution Layer:\n+    - [Stateless validation interfaces](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/blob/85fc20ca5937719a854472a87cb48d01ef1dffca/src/ethereum/forks/amsterdam/stateless.py)\n+    - [Guest program](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/blob/85fc20ca5937719a854472a87cb48d01ef1dffca/src/ethereum/forks/amsterdam/stateless_guest.py)\n+    - [Host-side input assembly](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/blob/85fc20ca5937719a854472a87cb48d01ef1dffca/src/ethereum/forks/amsterdam/stateless_host.py)\n+    - [Execution witness construction](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/blob/85fc20ca5937719a854472a87cb48d01ef1dffca/src/ethereum/forks/amsterdam/stateless_host_exec_witness.py)\n+    - [SSZ serialization schema](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/blob/85fc20ca5937719a854472a87cb48d01ef1dffca/src/ethereum/forks/amsterdam/stateless_ssz.py)\n+    - [Conformance tests](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/tree/85fc20ca5937719a854472a87cb48d01ef1dffca/tests/amsterdam/eip8025_optional_proofs)\n+\n+### Consensus Layer\n+\n+This EIP introduces a new `execution_proof` gossip topic on the\n+consensus-layer p2p network carrying `SignedExecutionProof` messages,\n+and a `ProofEngine` interface that beacon nodes use to generate and\n+verify execution proofs. Proof generation and\n+verification are delegated to an external proof node; the `ProofEngine`\n+is the in-client component that mediates communication with it. A node\n+MAY enable either or both of:\n+\n+- **Proof-generating mode.** An active validator that opts in to act as\n+  a _prover_ — produces execution proofs and broadcasts them on the\n+  `execution_proof` gossip topic.\n+- **Proof-verifying mode.** A node that consumes gossiped proofs and\n+  treats a verified proof as a supplementary attestation of the\n+  corresponding payload's validity. Proof verification does not require local\n+  EL state. Proof-verifying nodes still re-execute payloads themselves;\n+  verified proofs are an additional signal, not a replacement for\n+  re-execution. This separation lets clients deploy and measure the\n+  proving stack against live-network conditions without making\n+  fork-choice dependent on it. A subsequent EIP could propose promoting\n+  verified proofs to a load-bearing role and dropping re-execution once\n+  the stack has matured.\n+\n+The following diagram summarises how proofs move between the two roles:\n+\n+![Execution-proof flow between proof-generating and proof-verifying nodes via the `execution_proof` gossip topic](../assets/eip-8025/proof-flow.png)\n+\n+At a high level, the proof lifecycle is:\n+\n+1. A prover reacts to a new beacon block, constructs the corresponding\n+   `NewPayloadRequest`, and calls\n+   `proof_engine.request_proofs(new_payload_request, ProofAttributes(proof_types))`\n+   to initiate proof generation for its configured `proof_types` on the proof node.\n+2. The proof node produces an `ExecutionProof` for each requested type.\n+   The prover signs each proof using the `DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF` domain, wraps it in\n+   a `SignedExecutionProof`, and broadcasts it on the `execution_proof`\n+   topic.\n+3. Proof-verifying peers receive the gossip message, run the gossip\n+   validation rules, then call `proof_engine.verify_execution_proof` on\n+   the inner `ExecutionProof` to confirm payload validity.\n+\n+**Sync support requirement.** Independent of the request/produce/verify\n+loop above, every proof-aware node MUST retain valid proofs for\n+canonical-chain blocks back to the finalized checkpoint so that peers\n+syncing or filling gaps can backfill them via `ExecutionProofsByRange`\n+and `ExecutionProofsByRoot` (see [Req/resp domain](#reqresp-domain) for\n+the protocol details).\n+\n+#### Proof types and containers\n+\n+The consensus layer introduces a small set of new types and constants to\n+identify proofs, bound their size, and route gossip signatures:\n+\n+| Name                               | Value                      |\n+| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------- |\n+| `ProofType`                        | `uint8`                    |\n+| `MAX_PROOF_SIZE`                   | `409600` (= 400 KiB)       |\n+| `MAX_EXECUTION_PROOFS_PER_PAYLOAD` | `uint64(4)`                |\n+| `DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF`           | `DomainType('0x0D000000')` |\n+\n+`MAX_PROOF_SIZE` is set at `400 KiB` as a network-bandwidth budget: at the\n+gossip target of one proof per `(payload, proof_type)` and the cap of\n+`MAX_EXECUTION_PROOFS_PER_PAYLOAD = 4` proof types per payload, the\n+worst-case in-flight proof bandwidth per slot is `4 × 400 KiB = 1.6 MiB`\n+— of a similar order to existing per-slot blob-sidecar traffic. This\n+bounds steady-state traffic. Provers using systems that naturally\n+produce larger proofs are expected to apply proof compression\n+(recursion, succinct wrappers) before gossiping.\n+\n+Peers advertise their supported proof types via\n+`ExecutionProofStatus` (see [Req/resp domain](#reqresp-domain)). The set\n+of `proof_types` a node speaks is a per-node, dynamic configuration; new\n+proof systems can be added by socializing a new `ProofType` value\n+out-of-band and rolling it out to consenting operators. Because this EIP\n+is opt-in and changes no consensus rules, adding, deprecating, or\n+swapping proof systems does **not** require a hard fork or coordinated\n+client release — peers simply discover which proof types overlap during\n+their `ExecutionProofStatus` handshake and route requests accordingly.\n+\n+The top-level gossip message is the `SignedExecutionProof`:\n+\n+```python\n+class SignedExecutionProof(Container):\n+    message: ExecutionProof\n+    validator_index: ValidatorIndex\n+    signature: BLSSignature\n+```\n+\n+Its inner `ExecutionProof` couples a serialized proof blob to the proof\n+system and guest program it was generated against, and to the public\n+input that identifies the payload it certifies:\n+\n+```python\n+class ExecutionProof(Container):\n+    proof_data: ByteList[MAX_PROOF_SIZE]\n+    proof_type: ProofType\n+    public_input: PublicInput\n+\n+\n+class PublicInput(Container):\n+    new_payload_request_root: Root\n+    successful_validation: bool\n+    chain_config: ChainConfig\n+```\n+\n+The fields play the following roles:\n+\n+- `proof_data` is the proof system's serialized output. It is the only field\n+  whose size scales with the prover output and is bounded by\n+  `MAX_PROOF_SIZE`.\n+- `proof_type` selects which proof system and guest program the verifier dispatches to.\n+- `public_input.new_payload_request_root` is the SSZ `hash_tree_root` of the\n+  Engine API `NewPayloadRequest` whose execution this proof certifies. It is\n+  the link between a proof and a specific execution payload; verifiers use\n+  it to bind the proof to the payload they are verifying.\n+- `public_input.successful_validation` is `True` if the guest program\n+  accepted the payload as valid. Verifiers MUST check this field is\n+  `True` before treating the proof as a positive validity attestation.\n+- `public_input.chain_config` pins the chain ID and fork configuration the\n+  guest was run against, preventing cross-chain replay and fork\n+  mismatch. `ChainConfig` is defined in the\n+  [Execution Layer](#execution-layer) section.\n+- `validator_index` and `signature` identify the prover and prove that they\n+  signed the proof under `DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF`, allowing peers to\n+  attribute invalid proofs to a specific active validator.\n+\n+#### Proof engine interface\n+\n+The `ProofEngine` interface encapsulates the proof-system-specific logic\n+so that the consensus layer stays agnostic of which proof system is in\n+use. It acts as a payload-validity oracle for the beacon node, and its\n+API shape is modelled on the Engine API to allow for seamless\n+integration into the protocol. The `ProofEngine` is realized as an\n+in-client component that maintains its own proof state and delegates\n+the cryptographic work of proof generation and verification to an\n+external proof node, mirroring the way the `ExecutionEngine` delegates\n+payload execution to the EL client. The\n+interface comprises four operations and a `ProofAttributes` type:\n+\n+```python\n+def verify_execution_proof(\n+    self: ProofEngine,\n+    execution_proof: ExecutionProof,\n+) -> bool: ...\n+\n+\n+def notify_new_payload(\n+    self: ProofEngine,\n+    new_payload_request: NewPayloadRequest,\n+) -> None: ...\n+\n+\n+def notify_forkchoice_updated(\n+    self: ProofEngine,\n+    head_block_hash: Hash32,\n+    safe_block_hash: Hash32,\n+    finalized_block_hash: Hash32,\n+) -> None: ...\n+\n+\n+@dataclass\n+class ProofAttributes:\n+    proof_types: Sequence[ProofType]\n+\n+\n+def request_proofs(\n+    self: ProofEngine,\n+    new_payload_request: NewPayloadRequest,\n+    proof_attributes: ProofAttributes,\n+) -> Root: ...\n+```\n+\n+These operations decompose into three concerns:\n+\n+- **Verification** (`verify_execution_proof`) is called on every incoming\n+  proof that passes gossip validation. The engine performs the\n+  proof-system-specific cryptographic verification and binds the result\n+  to the specific payload identified by\n+  `proof.public_input.new_payload_request_root`. A payload is considered\n+  proof-verified once `k` valid `SignedExecutionProof`s for it have been\n+  verified. The value of `k` will be pinned before this EIP transitions\n+  to `Review`; it is intentionally left open while the network gathers\n+  real-world data.\n+  Peers exchange their current proof-verification view via\n+  `ExecutionProofStatus`.\n+- **Lifecycle notifications** (`notify_new_payload`,\n+  `notify_forkchoice_updated`) keep the engine in sync with the state\n+  of the beacon node. `notify_new_payload` lets the engine associate\n+  incoming proofs with the payloads they certify;\n+  `notify_forkchoice_updated` lets it track the canonical chain to\n+  drive proof retention and pruning.\n+- **Generation** (`request_proofs`) is used by proof-generating nodes to\n+  trigger asynchronous proof generation for a given payload and set of\n+  proof types. The return value is `new_payload_request.hash_tree_root()`,\n+  which the prover uses as a request id to correlate the proof-completion\n+  SSE event the proof node emits when a proof is ready to be fetched.\n+\n+#### Beacon-chain state transition\n+\n+EIP-8025 extends `process_block` to forward execution payload processing to\n+both the execution engine and the proof engine, and introduces a new\n+`process_execution_proof` handler for incoming proofs.\n+\n+`process_block` is modified to pass `PROOF_ENGINE` to\n+`process_execution_payload`:\n+\n+```python\n+def process_block(state: BeaconState, block: BeaconBlock) -> None:\n+    process_block_header(state, block)\n+    process_withdrawals(state, block.body.execution_payload)\n+    # [Modified in EIP8025]\n+    process_execution_payload(state, block.body, EXECUTION_ENGINE, PROOF_ENGINE)\n+    process_randao(state, block.body)\n+    process_eth1_data(state, block.body)\n+    process_operations(state, block.body)\n+    process_sync_aggregate(state, block.body.sync_aggregate)\n+```\n+\n+`process_execution_payload` is modified to additionally notify the proof\n+engine of the new payload after the execution engine has accepted it.\n+This hook lets the proof engine learn of each new payload so it\n+can associate it with the proofs that certify it as they arrive over\n+gossip:\n+\n+```python\n+def process_execution_payload(\n+    state: BeaconState,\n+    body: BeaconBlockBody,\n+    execution_engine: ExecutionEngine,\n+    proof_engine: ProofEngine,\n+) -> None:\n+    ...\n+    # Verify the execution payload is valid via ExecutionEngine\n+    assert execution_engine.verify_and_notify_new_payload(\n+        NewPayloadRequest(...)\n+    )\n+\n+    # [New in EIP8025]\n+    # Notify ProofEngine of the new execution payload\n+    proof_engine.notify_new_payload(NewPayloadRequest(...))\n+    ...\n+```\n+\n+A new `process_execution_proof` handles a `SignedExecutionProof` once it has\n+passed gossip validation. It re-checks that the prover is active in the\n+current state, verifies the BLS signature under `DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF`,\n+and delegates cryptographic verification to the proof engine:\n+\n+```python\n+def process_execution_proof(\n+    state: BeaconState,\n+    signed_proof: SignedExecutionProof,\n+    proof_engine: ProofEngine,\n+) -> None:\n+    proof_message = signed_proof.message\n+\n+    # Verify prover is an active validator\n+    validator = state.validators[signed_proof.validator_index]\n+    assert is_active_validator(validator, get_current_epoch(state))\n+\n+    domain = get_domain(state, DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF, compute_epoch_at_slot(state.slot))\n+    signing_root = compute_signing_root(proof_message, domain)\n+    assert bls.Verify(validator.pubkey, signing_root, signed_proof.signature)\n+\n+    # Verify the execution proof\n+    assert proof_engine.verify_execution_proof(proof_message)\n+```\n+\n+`process_execution_proof` is invoked outside the beacon-block state-transition\n+function and produces no on-chain state change: it is the operational hook\n+that lets a node decide whether to treat a gossiped proof as a valid\n+attestation of an execution payload. Proof storage is managed by the\n+`ProofEngine`; retention is bounded by `proof_serve_range` (see\n+[Req/resp domain](#reqresp-domain)): clients MUST retain proofs for\n+canonical-chain blocks\n+back to the finalized checkpoint so they can serve `ExecutionProofsByRange`\n+and `ExecutionProofsByRoot` requests.\n+\n+#### Proof gossip\n+\n+Execution proofs are gossiped over a new global topic, `execution_proof`,\n+carrying `SignedExecutionProof` messages. Each rule below is a libp2p\n+gossipsub validation rule, following the same `[IGNORE]` / `[REJECT]`\n+conventions used by the other beacon-node gossip topics. With\n+`proof = signed_execution_proof.message`:\n+\n+- _[IGNORE]_ the proof's `new_payload_request_root` has been seen via\n+  gossip or non-gossip sources (clients MAY queue proofs until the\n+  corresponding payload arrives).\n+- _[IGNORE]_ no _valid_ proof has already been received for the tuple\n+  `(new_payload_request_root, proof_type)` — i.e. only the first valid\n+  proof of each type per payload is forwarded.\n+- _[IGNORE]_ this is the first proof received for the tuple\n+  `(new_payload_request_root, proof_type, validator_index)` — i.e. each\n+  prover gets one shot per `(payload, proof_type)`.\n+- _[REJECT]_ the validator at `validator_index` is an active validator.\n+- _[REJECT]_ the BLS signature is valid for the prover's public key under\n+  `DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF`.\n+- _[REJECT]_ `proof.proof_data` is non-empty and no larger than\n+  `MAX_PROOF_SIZE`.\n+- _[REJECT]_ all of the checks in `process_execution_proof` pass.\n+\n+These rules compose with the existing gossipsub peer-scoring machinery: a\n+peer relaying messages that hit `[REJECT]` is downscored by the same\n+mechanism that scores misbehaviour on any other CL gossip topic. The\n+`[IGNORE]` rules bound steady-state bandwidth — once a node has a valid\n+proof for a given `(new_payload_request_root, proof_type)`, additional\n+proofs for the same tuple are dropped silently, regardless of who signs\n+them.\n+\n+#### Req/resp domain\n+\n+Three req/resp protocols let peers backfill, target, and coordinate proof\n+state:\n+\n+- **`ExecutionProofsByRange`** — request `(start_slot, count, proof_types)`,\n+  response `List[SignedExecutionProof]`. Mirrors `BlobSidecarsByRange` and\n+  `DataColumnSidecarsByRange`: range-based, root-unaware, filtered by proof\n+  type. Used for bulk backfill of proofs after a syncing window.\n+- **`ExecutionProofsByRoot`** — request `List[ProofByRootIdentifier]` where\n+  each identifier carries `(block_root, List[proof_type])`, response\n+  `List[SignedExecutionProof]`. Used for targeted retrieval when a node\n+  knows the specific block roots whose proofs it is missing.\n+- **`ExecutionProofStatus`** — request and response share the same\n+  container: `(block_root, slot, proof_types)`. Peers exchange the most\n+  recent block they consider proof-verified, plus their dynamically\n+  advertised set of supported proof types. The dialing peer MUST send a\n+  status on first connecting to any proof-aware peer. This is similar in\n+  nature to the beacon-chain\n+  [`Status v2`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/031e521f0a82b0e475ecfc13f79dd251a6284fc2/specs/fulu/p2p-interface.md#status-v2)\n+  handshake.\n+\n+Clients MUST serve both range and root requests for any block on the\n+canonical chain whose slot is in `proof_serve_range` — defined as\n+`[finalized_checkpoint.slot, current_slot]`. Peers unable to reply respond\n+with `3: ResourceUnavailable` and MAY be descored. The shape of these\n+protocols composes with existing sync flows: a node syncing forward over\n+blocks pulls proofs by range; a node patching a specific gap pulls them by\n+root.\n+\n+#### Discovery\n+\n+Discovery is extended with a new Ethereum Node Record (ENR) key, `eproof`, encoded as a `uint8`. A\n+node is considered proof-aware if the field is present and non-zero,\n+allowing other peers to filter for proof-aware peers during discovery. This\n+mirrors the existing pattern used to advertise data-column awareness in\n+Fulu via the\n+[`cgc` ENR field](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/031e521f0a82b0e475ecfc13f79dd251a6284fc2/specs/fulu/p2p-interface.md#the-discovery-domain-discv5)\n+and is intentionally cheap: no fork or fork-version bump is required for a\n+node to start (or stop) advertising proof support.\n+\n+#### Prover lifecycle\n+\n+The prover lifecycle is illustrated below:\n+\n+![Prover lifecycle: SSE-driven flow between beacon node, prover, and proof node](../assets/eip-8025/prover-lifecycle.png)\n+\n+A prover's flow, as detailed in the prover guide referenced above, is\n+fully event-driven:\n+\n+1. **Subscribe to two SSE event streams** at startup:\n+   - `Block` events from the beacon node, signalling that a new valid beacon\n+     block has been received.\n+   - Proof-completion events from the proof node.\n+2. **On a `Block` event**, fetch the full `BeaconBlock` via RPC, construct\n+   the corresponding `NewPayloadRequest`, choose the `ProofAttributes`\n+   (set of `proof_types` the prover wants to generate), and call\n+   `proof_engine.request_proofs(...)`. The returned root is used to track\n+   the request.\n+3. **On a proof-completion event** matching a tracked root, fetch the\n+   completed `ExecutionProof` from the proof node, sign it under\n+   `DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF`, wrap it in a `SignedExecutionProof`, and\n+   broadcast on the `execution_proof` gossip topic.\n+\n+The signing helper is:\n+\n+```python\n+def get_execution_proof_signature(\n+    state: BeaconState, proof: ExecutionProof, privkey: int\n+) -> BLSSignature:\n+    domain = get_domain(state, DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF, compute_epoch_at_slot(state.slot))\n+    signing_root = compute_signing_root(proof, domain)\n+    return bls.Sign(privkey, signing_root)\n+```\n+\n+The prover role is scoped to the optional-proof phase. If a future EIP\n+were to make execution proofs mandatory, proof generation would\n+plausibly move into block production, at which point the prover role\n+and the optional gossip topic could be deprecated in favour of\n+in-block proof commitments.\n+\n+### Execution Layer\n+\n+This EIP introduces a stateless execution guest and prover side logic to construct the input used by\n+that guest. The prover runs the guest over private `StatelessInput` bytes. The\n+proof exposes `StatelessValidationResult` as public output, allowing a verifier\n+to bind the proof to the payload request being checked.\n+\n+A proof-verifying node accepts the execution-layer result only if:\n+\n+- the proof verifies for the expected guest program;\n+- `successful_validation` is `true`;\n+- `new_payload_request_root` equals the SSZ `hash_tree_root` of the\n+  `NewPayloadRequest` associated with the payload being validated; and\n+- `chain_config` matches the chain ID and fork configuration expected by the\n+  verifier.\n+\n+At a high level, proof generation follows this flow:\n+\n+1. A host, usually a stateful execution-layer client, executes or constructs\n+   the block while recording the account, storage, code, and ancestor-header\n+   data used during execution.\n+2. The host builds an `ExecutionWitness`, wraps it with the Engine API\n+   `NewPayloadRequest`, chain configuration, and transaction public keys into a\n+   `StatelessInput`, and serializes that input as schema-prefixed SSZ bytes.\n+3. A prover runs the guest program on the serialized `StatelessInput`. The\n+   guest validates the chain configuration and witness scaffolding, executes the\n+   payload against witness-backed state, and returns `StatelessValidationResult`.\n+\n+#### Stateless input and output\n+\n+The top-level guest input is private prover input:\n+\n+```python\n+class StatelessInput:\n+    new_payload_request: NewPayloadRequest\n+    witness: ExecutionWitness\n+    chain_config: ChainConfig\n+    public_keys: Tuple[Bytes, ...]\n+```\n+\n+The guest output is public:\n+\n+```python\n+class StatelessValidationResult:\n+    new_payload_request_root: Hash32\n+    successful_validation: bool\n+    chain_config: ChainConfig\n+```\n+\n+Note this struct is the EL-counterpart of `PublicInput` described in the _Proof types and containers_\n+section.\n+\n+At this level:\n+\n+- `new_payload_request` is the Engine API payload data supplied by the\n+  consensus layer.\n+- `witness` is the account, storage, code, and ancestor-header data needed to\n+  execute the payload without local EL state.\n+- `chain_config` tells the guest which chain ID and fork configuration to\n+  validate against.\n+- `public_keys` contains one 65-byte uncompressed secp256k1 public key for\n+  each transaction signer, in the same order as the transactions in the payload.\n+  Optimized guests can use these keys to avoid public-key recovery, but\n+  transaction signatures and supplied public keys MUST still be verified.\n+\n+The `NewPayloadRequest` commits to the payload, blob versioned hashes,\n+`parent_beacon_block_root`, and typed execution requests:\n+\n+```python\n+class NewPayloadRequest:\n+    execution_payload: ExecutionPayload\n+    versioned_hashes: Tuple[VersionedHash, ...]\n+    parent_beacon_block_root: Root\n+    execution_requests: ExecutionRequests\n+\n+\n+class ExecutionPayload:\n+    parent_hash: Hash32\n+    fee_recipient: Address\n+    state_root: Root\n+    receipts_root: Root\n+    logs_bloom: Bloom\n+    prev_randao: Bytes32\n+    block_number: Uint\n+    gas_limit: Uint\n+    gas_used: Uint\n+    timestamp: U256\n+    extra_data: Bytes\n+    base_fee_per_gas: Uint\n+    block_hash: Hash32\n+    transactions: Tuple[Bytes, ...]\n+    withdrawals: Tuple[Withdrawal, ...]\n+    blob_gas_used: U64\n+    excess_blob_gas: U64\n+    block_access_list: Bytes\n+```\n+\n+The execution requests are represented as typed containers, matching the\n+consensus-layer specs:\n+\n+```python\n+class DepositRequest:\n+    pubkey: Bytes48\n+    withdrawal_credentials: Bytes32\n+    amount: U64\n+    signature: Bytes96\n+    index: U64\n+\n \n-Validators will now be able to enable two new modes:\n+class WithdrawalRequest:\n+    source_address: Address\n+    validator_pubkey: Bytes48\n+    amount: U64\n \n-- zkEVM Proof generating\n-- Stateless validation\n \n-When a proof generating node receives a beacon block, they will create the necessary proofs for the execution payload in the block and re-propagate them on the specified subnets.\n+class ConsolidationRequest:\n+    source_address: Address\n+    source_pubkey: Bytes48\n+    target_pubkey: Bytes48\n \n-When a stateless validating node receives a beacon block, they will check to see if they have already received a valid execution proof for that execution payload from the specified subnet.\n \n-The detailed specifications are in the consensus-specs repository.\n+class ExecutionRequests:\n+    deposits: Tuple[DepositRequest, ...]\n+    withdrawals: Tuple[WithdrawalRequest, ...]\n+    consolidations: Tuple[ConsolidationRequest, ...]\n+```\n \n-The key words \"MUST\", \"MUST NOT\", \"REQUIRED\", \"SHALL\", \"SHALL NOT\", \"SHOULD\", \"SHOULD NOT\", \"RECOMMENDED\", \"NOT RECOMMENDED\", \"MAY\", and \"OPTIONAL\" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119 and RFC 8174.\n+The remaining top-level fields define the witness and chain context consumed by\n+the guest:\n+\n+```python\n+class ExecutionWitness:\n+    state: Tuple[Bytes, ...]\n+    codes: Tuple[Bytes, ...]\n+    headers: Tuple[Bytes, ...]\n+\n+\n+class ChainConfig:\n+    chain_id: U64\n+    active_fork: ForkConfig\n+\n+\n+class ForkConfig:\n+    fork: ProtocolFork\n+    activation: ForkActivation\n+    blob_schedule: BlobSchedule | None\n+\n+\n+class ForkActivation:\n+    block_number: U64 | None\n+    timestamp: U64 | None\n+\n+\n+class BlobSchedule:\n+    target: U64\n+    max: U64\n+    base_fee_update_fraction: U64\n+\n+\n+class ProtocolFork(StrEnum):\n+    ...\n+    Amsterdam = \"Amsterdam\"\n+```\n+\n+The `ExecutionWitness` fields have the following roles:\n+\n+- `state`: RLP-encoded account and storage trie-node preimages needed during\n+  execution and state-root recomputation.\n+- `codes`: bytecodes required for code reads from the pre-state. Code created\n+  in the block being executed is not included because the guest observes it\n+  during re-execution.\n+- `headers`: RLP-encoded parent and ancestor headers, ordered by block number\n+  and ending at the payload parent. These headers provide the parent state root\n+  and the recent block hashes used by `BLOCKHASH` and system-contract logic.\n+  The guest checks that the headers form a contiguous chain.\n+\n+#### Guest validation\n+\n+The guest entry point decodes schema-prefixed SSZ input, runs stateless payload \n+validation, and serializes the result.\n+\n+```python\n+def run_stateless_guest(input_bytes: Bytes) -> Bytes:\n+    stateless_input = deserialize_stateless_input(input_bytes)\n+    stateless_output = verify_stateless_new_payload(stateless_input)\n+    return serialize_stateless_output(stateless_output)\n+```\n+\n+The main validation path first computes the public payload-request commitment.\n+It then validates fork configuration, checks the header witness, creates a\n+`WitnessState`, and delegates payload execution to the same `new_payload` path\n+used by the execution engine:\n+\n+```python\n+def compute_new_payload_request_root(\n+    stateless_input: StatelessInput,\n+) -> Hash32:\n+    ssz_npr = _new_payload_request_to_ssz(stateless_input.new_payload_request)\n+    return Hash32(ssz_npr.hash_tree_root())\n+\n+\n+def validate_chain_config(\n+    chain_config: ChainConfig,\n+    new_payload_request: NewPayloadRequest,\n+) -> ForkConfig:\n+    active_fork = chain_config.active_fork\n+    execution_payload = new_payload_request.execution_payload\n+\n+    if not _is_activation_active(active_fork.activation, execution_payload):\n+        raise InactiveForkConfigError(...)\n+    if active_fork.fork not in guest_supported_forks():\n+        raise UnsupportedForkConfigError(...)\n+    if active_fork.blob_schedule != _expected_amsterdam_blob_schedule():\n+        raise UnsupportedForkConfigError(...)\n+\n+    return active_fork\n+\n+\n+def validate_headers(\n+    encoded_headers: Tuple[Bytes, ...],\n+) -> Tuple[List[Header | PreviousForkHeader], List[Hash32]]:\n+    assert len(encoded_headers) <= 256\n+    headers = [_decode_header(header) for header in encoded_headers]\n+    block_hashes = [keccak256(header) for header in encoded_headers]\n+    for i in range(1, len(headers)):\n+        if headers[i].parent_hash != block_hashes[i - 1]:\n+            raise Exception(\"Witness headers are not contiguous\")\n+    return headers, block_hashes\n+\n+\n+def verify_stateless_new_payload(\n+    stateless_input: StatelessInput,\n+) -> StatelessValidationResult:\n+    new_payload_request_root = compute_new_payload_request_root(\n+        stateless_input\n+    )\n+    witness = stateless_input.witness\n+\n+    try:\n+        validate_chain_config(\n+            stateless_input.chain_config,\n+            stateless_input.new_payload_request,\n+        )\n+\n+        decoded_headers, block_hashes = validate_headers(witness.headers)\n+        parent_header = decoded_headers[-1]\n+\n+        chain_context = ChainContext(\n+            chain_id=stateless_input.chain_config.chain_id,\n+            block_hashes=block_hashes,\n+            parent_header=parent_header,\n+        )\n+\n+        pre_state = WitnessState(\n+            _node_db=build_node_db(witness.state),\n+            _state_root=parent_header.state_root,\n+            _code_db=build_code_db(witness.codes),\n+        )\n+\n+        execute_new_payload_request(\n+            stateless_input.new_payload_request,\n+            pre_state,\n+            chain_context,\n+            transaction_public_keys=stateless_input.public_keys,\n+        )\n+        successful_validation = True\n+    except Exception:\n+        successful_validation = False\n+\n+    return StatelessValidationResult(\n+        new_payload_request_root=new_payload_request_root,\n+        successful_validation=successful_validation,\n+        chain_config=stateless_input.chain_config,\n+    )\n+```\n+\n+`WitnessState` is the stateless replacement for a local pre-state database. It\n+serves account, storage, and code reads from the witness and computes the\n+post-state root from the execution diff:\n+\n+```python\n+class WitnessState:\n+    _node_db: Dict[Bytes, Bytes]\n+    _state_root: Root\n+    _code_db: Dict[Hash32, Bytes]\n+\n+    def get_account_optional(self, address: Address) -> Optional[Account]: ...\n+    def get_storage(self, address: Address, key: Bytes32) -> U256: ...\n+    def get_code(self, code_hash: Hash32) -> Bytes: ...\n+\n+    def compute_state_root_and_trie_changes(\n+        self,\n+        account_changes: Dict[Address, Optional[Account]],\n+        storage_changes: Dict[Address, Dict[Bytes32, U256]],\n+    ) -> Tuple[Root, List[InternalNode]]:\n+        ...\n+```\n+\n+The payload execution logic performs the normal payload checks before\n+executing the block:\n+\n+```python\n+def execute_new_payload_request(\n+    new_payload_request: NewPayloadRequest,\n+    pre_state: PreState,\n+    chain_context: ChainContext,\n+    transaction_public_keys: Optional[Tuple[Bytes, ...]] = None,\n+) -> Tuple[BlockDiff, Block]:\n+    payload = new_payload_request.execution_payload\n+\n+    if b\"\" in payload.transactions:\n+        raise InvalidBlock(\"Empty transaction in payload\")\n+    if not is_valid_block_hash(\n+        payload,\n+        new_payload_request.parent_beacon_block_root,\n+        new_payload_request.execution_requests,\n+    ):\n+        raise InvalidBlock(\"Invalid block hash\")\n+    if not is_valid_versioned_hashes(new_payload_request):\n+        raise InvalidBlock(\"Invalid versioned hashes\")\n+\n+    block = _payload_block(\n+        payload,\n+        new_payload_request.parent_beacon_block_root,\n+        new_payload_request.execution_requests,\n+    )\n+    block_diff = execute_block(\n+        block,\n+        pre_state,\n+        chain_context,\n+        transaction_public_keys=transaction_public_keys,\n+    )\n+    return block_diff, block\n+```\n+\n+During transaction processing, supplied public keys are verified before deriving\n+sender addresses:\n+\n+```python\n+def recover_sender_from_public_key(\n+    chain_id: U64,\n+    tx: Transaction,\n+    public_key: Bytes,\n+) -> Address:\n+    if public_key != recover_transaction_public_key(chain_id, tx):\n+        raise InvalidSignatureError\n+    return _sender_address_from_public_key(public_key)\n+```\n+\n+Optimized guests may avoid full public-key recovery, but they must still verify\n+that the supplied key validates the transaction signature and is consistent with\n+the recovery id or y-parity bit.\n+\n+#### Host-side input construction\n+\n+On the host side, `build_stateless_input` receives the artefacts gathered during\n+block execution or construction and packages them for the guest:\n+\n+```python\n+def build_stateless_input(\n+    block: Block,\n+    *,\n+    execution_witness: ExecutionWitness,\n+    execution_requests: ExecutionRequests,\n+    block_access_list: BlockAccessList,\n+    chain_id: U64,\n+) -> StatelessInput:\n+    ...\n+\n+    new_payload = NewPayloadRequest(\n+        execution_payload=payload,\n+        versioned_hashes=tuple(versioned_hashes),\n+        parent_beacon_block_root=header.parent_beacon_block_root,\n+        execution_requests=execution_requests,\n+    )\n+\n+    return StatelessInput(\n+        new_payload_request=new_payload,\n+        witness=execution_witness,\n+        chain_config=build_chain_config(chain_id),\n+        public_keys=tuple(public_keys),\n+    )\n+```\n+\n+The host also provides the fork configuration corresponding to the payload being\n+validated:\n+\n+```python\n+def build_chain_config(chain_id: U64) -> ChainConfig:\n+    return ChainConfig(\n+        chain_id=chain_id,\n+        active_fork=ForkConfig(\n+            fork=ProtocolFork.Amsterdam,\n+            activation=ForkActivation(\n+                block_number=None,\n+                timestamp=U64(0),\n+            ),\n+            blob_schedule=BlobSchedule(\n+                target=BLOB_SCHEDULE_TARGET,\n+                max=BLOB_SCHEDULE_MAX,\n+                base_fee_update_fraction=U64(BLOB_BASE_FEE_UPDATE_FRACTION),\n+            ),\n+        ),\n+    )\n+```\n+\n+The execution witness is built from the block-level read/write tracker and\n+pre-state trie data. The read/write tracker is a component already used in ELs\n+to track which data is touched during execution to assist for block access list (BALs)\n+construction. Conceptually, witness construction:\n+\n+1. collects the parent header and any older ancestors touched by `BLOCKHASH`;\n+2. collects pre-state bytecode reads;\n+3. captures account and storage trie nodes needed for all reads and writes;\n+4. captures any potential sibling requires because of branch compression\n+   during post-state root calculation.\n+\n+```python\n+def build_execution_witness(\n+    block_state: BlockState,\n+    expected_post_state_root: Root,\n+    pre_state_accounts_data: Trie[Address, Optional[Account]],\n+    pre_state_storages_data: Dict[Address, Trie[Bytes32, U256]],\n+    blockchain_headers: Optional[List[Bytes]] = None,\n+) -> ExecutionWitness:\n+    ancestor_headers = get_witness_ancestors(\n+        blockchain_headers if blockchain_headers is not None else [],\n+        block_state.oldest_ancestor_offset,\n+    )\n+    codes = get_witness_codes(block_state.code_reads, block_state.pre_state)\n+\n+    incr_storage_mpts = _build_pre_state_storage_mpts(pre_state_storages_data)\n+    incr_account_mpt = _build_pre_state_account_mpt(\n+        pre_state_accounts_data, incr_storage_mpts\n+    )\n+\n+    all_storage_accesses = _collect_storage_accesses(block_state)\n+    _capture_pre_state_storage_nodes(incr_storage_mpts, all_storage_accesses)\n+    _apply_storage_writes(incr_storage_mpts, block_state.storage_writes)\n+\n+    all_dirty_accounts = _get_all_dirty_accounts(block_state)\n+    _capture_pre_state_account_nodes(\n+        incr_account_mpt,\n+        block_state.account_reads,\n+        all_dirty_accounts,\n+    )\n+    _apply_account_writes(\n+        incr_account_mpt,\n+        incr_storage_mpts,\n+        block_state,\n+        all_dirty_accounts,\n+    )\n+\n+    assert mpt_root(incr_account_mpt) == expected_post_state_root\n+\n+    accessed_nodes = _collect_accessed_nodes(\n+        incr_account_mpt, incr_storage_mpts\n+    )\n+\n+    return ExecutionWitness(\n+        state=tuple(sorted(accessed_nodes.values())),\n+        codes=tuple(codes),\n+        headers=tuple(ancestor_headers),\n+    )\n+```\n+\n+#### SSZ encoding\n+\n+The host serializes a `StatelessInput` by prefixing the SSZ bytes with\n+`STATELESS_INPUT_SCHEMA_ID`. This lets future guest programs select the correct\n+input schema as forks or encoding rules evolve.\n+\n+```python\n+STATELESS_INPUT_SCHEMA_ID = 0x0001\n+STATELESS_INPUT_SCHEMA_ID_SIZE = 2\n+\n+\n+def serialize_stateless_input(\n+    stateless_input: StatelessInput,\n+) -> Bytes:\n+    ssz_obj = stateless_input_to_ssz(stateless_input)\n+    return Bytes(\n+        STATELESS_INPUT_SCHEMA_ID_BYTES +
